1.name: first person
1.plain: the speaker: I, we two, we

3.name: third person
3.plain: anyone or anything else: he, she, it, they

DU.name: dual
DU.plain: exactly two; Sanskrit has separate forms for a pair

PL.name: plural
PL.plain: three or more (two takes the dual)

N.name: neuter
N.plain: one of the three genders; its nominative and accusative are always alike

NOM.name: nominative
NOM.plain: the case of the subject, and of a noun that says what the subject is

ACC.name: accusative
ACC.plain: the case of the direct object, and of the goal of motion

INS.name: instrumental
INS.plain: the case of the means, the companion and the agent: with, by

DAT.name: dative
DAT.plain: the case of the person or purpose something is for: to, for

ABL.name: ablative
ABL.plain: the case of the starting point or cause: from, because of

GEN.name: genitive
GEN.plain: the case of the owner or whole: of, 's

LOC.name: locative
LOC.plain: the case of place and time: in, on, at, among, when

VOC.name: vocative
VOC.plain: the form used to call or address someone

Q.name: question particle
Q.plain: a word that turns a statement into a yes/no question

EMPH.name: emphatic particle
EMPH.plain: a word (eva) that puts weight on the word before it: only, just that, indeed

QUOT.name: quotative
QUOT.plain: the word iti, which closes a quotation or a thought

DEM.name: demonstrative
DEM.plain: a pointing word: that, this; also used for he, she, it

MID.name: middle voice
MID.plain: a set of verb endings that often means the action is done for or to oneself

PST.name: past
PST.plain: the augment a-, a prefix that puts a verb in past time; also marks past participles

IMP.name: imperative
IMP.plain: the verb form for commands and requests

OPT.name: optative
OPT.plain: the verb form for wishes, rules, advice and what would or could happen

PTCP.name: participle
PTCP.plain: a verb form that works as an adjective

ACT.name: active
ACT.plain: marks the active past participle in -tavat (having done), as opposed to the passive one in -ta

PASS.name: passive
PASS.plain: a verb form whose subject undergoes the action

CVB.name: converb (absolutive)
CVB.plain: an unchanging verb form meaning 'having done', linking one action to the main verb; Indologists call it the absolutive or gerund

INF.name: infinitive
INF.plain: the verb form in -tum: to do

FUT.name: future
FUT.plain: the verb forms for what will happen

PRF.name: perfect
PRF.plain: the reduplicated past tense of the epics and of narrative

AOR.name: aorist
AOR.plain: a past tense built on its own stem; in Classical Sanskrit rarer than the imperfect

PROH.name: prohibitive
PROH.plain: the word mā, 'do not', used with an unaugmented aorist or an imperative

PRS.name: present
PRS.plain: marks the present participle (doing), as opposed to the past one

INDF.name: indefinite
INDF.plain: the particles cid, cana and api after a question word, making it 'some-' or (with a negative) 'any-'

REL.name: relative
REL.plain: the stem ya-: who, which, the one that

COND.name: conditional
COND.plain: a rare verb form for a condition that did not or will not happen: would have done

GDV.name: gerundive
GDV.plain: a verbal adjective meaning 'to be done, that must be done'

CAUS.name: causative
CAUS.plain: a verb form meaning 'make or let someone do'

DESID.name: desiderative
DESID.plain: a verb form meaning 'want to do'

INTS.name: intensive
INTS.plain: a verb form meaning 'do repeatedly or hard'

DENOM.name: denominative
DENOM.plain: a verb made from a noun: 'act like, treat as, wish for'

PREC.name: precative
PREC.plain: a rare optative of the aorist used for blessings: may it be

SBJV.name: subjunctive
SBJV.plain: a Vedic verb form for will and expectation; in Classical Sanskrit it survives only in the first-person imperative
